back: A tax on income or wealth paid directly to the government by the person or firm that bears it, such as income tax or corporate tax.
A tax on spending on goods and services, collected by sellers, such as VAT, excise and customs duties.
A tax whose average rate (percentage of income paid) rises as income rises.
A tax that takes a smaller percentage of income as income rises, falling most heavily on the poor.
A tax that takes the same percentage of income at every income level.

front: What is the difference between an **ad valorem** and a **specific** tax?
back: Ad valorem: a percentage of the price (e.g. VAT). Specific: a fixed amount per unit (e.g. US\$0.25 per litre).
Raise revenue; redistribute income; discourage demerit goods and pollution; protect domestic industries; manage aggregate demand.

front: Name four canons (principles) of a good tax.
back: Equity (ability to pay), certainty, convenience and economy of collection.
